properties.notes: Source classifies this as "Data centre-targeted employment land", status "discussion". Size: approx. 25 acres across multiple parcels (company-stated). This site has been raised publicly through operator marketing, media coverage, or community reports. As of July 2026, no formal planning application has been filed with the Town of Oakville. Inclusion is for transparency, not confirmation. On May 18, 2026, HIVE Digital Technologies Ltd. announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, BUZZ High Performance Computing Inc., is planning an industrial-scale AI infrastructure facility in the Greater Toronto Area with approximately 320 MW of utility capacity, a target of second half 2027, and an investment described at approximately CAD $3.5 billion. The company describes the facility as using closed-loop cooling with a no-water-use approach. The May release identified the location only as being within the Toronto-Waterloo corridor. A commercial real estate listing for an adjacent parcel subsequently identified 3480 Ninth Line in north Oakville as the site, and this location was reported by Oakville News in July 2026. The Town of Oakville has confirmed in writing that, as of July 17, 2026, it is aware lands may be under consideration by a proponent for a data centre, but that no development application has been submitted and, as a result, the statutory public planning process has not commenced. No zoning amendment, Official Plan amendment, pre-consultation record, or IESO connection filing tied to this address has been located in public records. Facility specifications, including capacity, cooling type, cost, and timeline, are drawn from the company’s own announcement and have not been reviewed or confirmed through any municipal planning process, because no application has been filed. Primary source cited by the tracker: https://www.oakville.ca/town-hall/news-notices/2026-news-releases-archive/town-of-oakville-responds-to-data-centre-inquiries/ ; https://www.hivedigitaltechnologies.com/news/hives-buzz-hpc-announces-320-mw-sovereign-ai-infrastructure-in-greater-toronto-area/?utm_source=oakville%20news&utm_campaign=oakville%20news%3A%20outbound&utm_medium=referral

SPUR Innovation (Waterloo-based) has publicly confirmed early evaluation of the 25-acre property for a possible AI data centre campus, potentially including a vertical farm and greenhouse. The property is the former Wolverine Tube copper tubing plant, a 165,000-square-foot industrial building constructed in 1986. It is owned by 1623242 Ontario Inc., a numbered corporation listing SPUR founder Krishan (Kapley) Judge as director. A concept website, since removed, described a three-phase development: phase one at 25 to 35 MW over up to three years, phase two at 50 to 75 MW over three to five years, and a potential phase three expanding to adjacent land at 150 to 300 MW over more than five years. The website referenced closed-loop cooling and a vertical farm component. These figures are operator claims from marketing materials, not planning documents. The property is zoned M2 General Industrial under the Township of Centre Wellington's zoning by-law. Data centres and AI data centres are not currently listed as permitted uses in the Township's zoning by-laws or Official Plan, nor in the County of Wellington's. SPUR's principals have publicly stated that if the project were to move beyond the evaluation stage, SPUR would work through applicable planning, environmental, and regulatory processes and participate in public consultation. As of the most recent review, no planning application, site plan, or pre-consultation record appears on the Township's planning portal. A planning inquiry has been sent to Centre Wellington; no formal response has been received. Size: TOR01B/C: approx. 39,900 m² combined office and data halls (planning file); TOR01A: 158,000 sq ft (per operator materials). Three-building campus on approximately 19 acres at the northwest corner of Danforth Ave and Birchmount Rd; former Eli Lilly Canada headquarters site. Developed in partnership with First Gulf; WZMH Architects; MEP and civil by Stantec. TOR01A (8 MW, renovated existing building) appears operational. TOR01B and TOR01C: Notice of Approval Conditions issued September 23, 2025; Statement of Approval not yet issued — conditionally approved, not finally approved. Total critical capacity: 56 MW per the project noise study — 8 MW for TOR01A; 48 MW combined for TOR01B and TOR01C. The 24 MW per-building split is per operator materials, not the planning file. Cooling: data halls were originally designed for an evaporative cooling system; design subsequently changed to air-cooled chillers per engineering filings (Morrison Hershfield and Ramboll, 2024–2025). Backup power: 35 diesel backup generators planned for the new buildings — 33 at 3,000 kW and 2 at 750 kW — per the project's 2023 noise study. The noise study models compliance with City sound limits conditional on 5-metre acoustic walls and generators being used for emergency backup only; more regular generator use would require separate provincial approval and potentially additional mitigation. Use classification: City confirmed the use is permitted through the Core Employment designation under the Toronto Official Plan (Section 4.6); site plan control was the appropriate approval path. No public IESO connection filing has been located for this site. TOR01A appears operational. Construction on TOR01B and TOR01C: not confirmed. The following details are per operator materials and do not appear in the planning file reviewed: Toronto Hydro three-substation arrangement, ISO 9001/PCI DSS/SSAE 18 certifications, and Q2 2026 delivery date. The new buildings (TOR01B/C) comprise approximately 39,900 m² of office and data halls per the planning file; floor area figures in square feet are per operator materials.
